details:
Description

After joining a world in VRChat, the Windows system process csrss.exe starts continuously accumulating private memory. The growth stops after I exit VRChat.

The affected process is csrss.exe, not VRChat.exe. I would expect its memory usage to stabilize during normal gameplay rather than continue increasing over time.

Examples measured on October 29, 2026 (UTC+8):

- 20:11:47–20:12:17: csrss.exe private memory increased from 33.90 MiB to 35.46 MiB.

- 20:15:53–20:16:23: it increased from 59.56 MiB to 60.11 MiB, even after removing my CPU affinity launch arguments.

The second csrss.exe process remained stable at approximately 2.69 MiB during both samples.

I normally use CPU affinity launch arguments on my dual-CCD CPU. However, I also reproduced the issue after removing both --affinity=0x5555 and --user-affinity. It also reproduces in desktop mode.

I am currently not observing this behavior in other Easy Anti-Cheat games on the same PC. I do not know whether the underlying cause is VRChat, EAC, Windows, or an interaction between them.

System information:

- CPU: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D

- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti

- OS: Windows 11 25H2, build 26200.9457

- VRChat: 2026.4.1, build 1936, Steam public branch

A previous Windows update appeared to stop this behavior temporarily, but it has now returned on the same Windows build. I cannot confirm exactly when it returned or whether a particular VRChat update caused it.

Reproduction Steps

Steps to reproduce:

1. Launch VRChat on Windows.

2. Monitor the Private Bytes / private memory usage of the csrss.exe processes.

3. Join a world and remain in it.

4. Observe that one csrss.exe process continues increasing its private memory usage over time.

5. Exit VRChat. The continuous growth stops.

I repeated the test after removing my CPU affinity launch arguments, and the memory growth still occurred.

Temporary workaround:

Exiting VRChat stops further growth. Restarting Windows previously reset the accumulated csrss.exe memory usage, but this does not prevent the issue from recurring.

I have not found a permanent workaround.
